sets.title: Puzzle 11: 4 lectures between Monday and Thursday
sets.text:
A college schedules 4 lectures (Economics, Chemistry, History, English) on 4 different days between Monday and Thursday, one lecture per day. Conditions:
1. The Economics lecture is not on Monday.
2. The English lecture is held on the day immediately after the History lecture.
3. The History lecture is not on Monday.
4. The English lecture is not on Thursday.

sets.title: Puzzle 12: 4 lectures between Tuesday and Friday
sets.text:
4 people (Omkar, Uma, Priya, Rohit) each have a lecture with a manager, on 4 different days between Tuesday and Friday, at most one per day. Conditions:
1. Uma's lecture is on a later day than Omkar's.
2. Exactly 2 days separate the lectures of Omkar and Priya.
3. Uma's lecture is not on Wednesday.

sets.title: Puzzle 13: 4 lectures between Monday and Friday
sets.text:
A college schedules 4 lectures (History, Biology, English, Economics) on 4 different days between Monday and Friday, one lecture per day, so exactly one day in this period has no lecture. Conditions:
1. Exactly 2 days separate the English lecture and the Biology lecture.
2. Exactly 3 days separate the Economics lecture and the Biology lecture.
3. The History lecture is held on the day immediately after the English lecture.

sets.title: Puzzle 14: 5 lectures between Tuesday and Sunday
sets.text:
A college schedules 5 lectures (English, Maths, Economics, Chemistry, Computer Science) on 5 different days between Tuesday and Sunday, one lecture per day, so exactly one day in this period has no lecture. Conditions:
1. The Maths lecture is held either on Wednesday or on Tuesday.
2. The Chemistry lecture is held on the day immediately after the Maths lecture.
3. The Chemistry lecture is held on a later day than the Economics lecture.
4. The Computer Science lecture is not on Sunday.
5. The English lecture is held on Saturday.

sets.title: Puzzle 15: 5 lectures between Tuesday and Sunday
sets.text:
A college schedules 5 lectures (Maths, History, English, Biology, Chemistry) on 5 different days between Tuesday and Sunday, one lecture per day, so exactly one day in this period has no lecture. Conditions:
1. The English lecture is held either on Tuesday or on Wednesday.
2. The Biology lecture is held on Sunday.
3. The History lecture is held on a later day than the Maths lecture.
4. The English lecture is held on a later day than the Chemistry lecture.
5. Exactly 1 day separates the Maths lecture and the English lecture.

sets.title: Puzzle 16: 5 meetings between Monday and Saturday
sets.text:
5 people (Mohan, Ishita, Jayant, Jagan, Lakshmi) each have a meeting with a manager, on 5 different days between Monday and Saturday, at most one per day, leaving exactly one day free. Conditions:
1. Ishita's meeting is on Monday or Tuesday.
2. Mohan's meeting is on the day immediately after Jagan's.
3. Lakshmi's meeting is on Tuesday.
4. Jagan's meeting is on Thursday or Tuesday.
5. Jagan's meeting is on the day immediately after Jayant's.

sets.title: Puzzle 17: 5 visits between Monday and Saturday
sets.text:
5 people (Imran, Divya, Balaji, Dinesh, Omkar) each have a visit with a manager, on 5 different days between Monday and Saturday, at most one per day, leaving exactly one day free. Conditions:
1. Divya's visit is on Monday or Thursday.
2. Omkar's visit is on a later day than Balaji's.
3. Dinesh's visit is on Wednesday.
4. Exactly 3 days separate the visits of Imran and Divya.
5. Balaji's visit is on the day immediately after Dinesh's.

sets.title: Puzzle 18: 5 visits between Tuesday and Sunday
sets.text:
5 people (Pranav, Balaji, Arjun, Ramesh, Bharat) each have a visit with a manager, on 5 different days between Tuesday and Sunday, at most one per day, leaving exactly one day free. Conditions:
1. Bharat's visit is on the day immediately after Ramesh's.
2. Arjun's visit is on Tuesday.
3. Pranav's visit is not on Friday.
4. Ramesh's visit is on Saturday.
5. Balaji's visit is on Sunday or Thursday.

sets.title: Puzzle 19: 6 lectures between Monday and Sunday
sets.text:
A college schedules 6 lectures (Economics, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, History, Maths) on 6 different days between Monday and Sunday, one lecture per day, so exactly one day in this period has no lecture. Conditions:
1. The Computer Science lecture is held on the day immediately after the Maths lecture.
2. The Maths lecture is held on Wednesday.
3. The Chemistry lecture is held on a later day than the History lecture.
4. The Physics lecture is held on Sunday.
5. The Economics lecture is held on the day immediately after the History lecture.
6. The Chemistry lecture is held either on Saturday or on Tuesday.

sets.title: Puzzle 20: 6 meetings between Monday and Sunday
sets.text:
6 people (Nandini, Tarun, Farhan, Lakshmi, Chitra, Manoj) each have a meeting with a manager, on 6 different days between Monday and Sunday, at most one per day, leaving exactly one day free. Conditions:
1. Exactly 3 days separate the meetings of Manoj and Chitra.
2. Manoj's meeting is on a later day than Farhan's.
3. Manoj's meeting is on Wednesday or Thursday.
4. Farhan's meeting is on the day immediately after Nandini's.
5. Tarun's meeting is on Saturday or Sunday.
6. Lakshmi's meeting is on Monday or Friday.
